title: Regulatory Lag on Emerging Technologies
bottleneck: Regulators consistently trail technological change — approving too slowly for beneficial innovations (advanced nuclear, cultivated meat, autonomous systems) while lacking frameworks for novel risks. The lag is structural: agencies lack technical capacity and face asymmetric blame for approvals versus delays. Agencies optimized for stability cannot match the pace of fields like AI and synthetic biology.
why_it_blocks: Slow, uncertain regulation both delays beneficial deployment and leaves real risks ungoverned. Both under-regulation of risks and over-regulation of benefits stem from the same lag.
current_state: Regulatory sandboxes and adaptive licensing are piloted in pockets, but most agencies still operate on decades-old frameworks. Outcome-based regulation and sandboxes are promising but remain exceptional rather than standard practice. Agencies need new operating models built for the pace of modern technology.
